top_stories.title: Bitcoin Falls Below $60,000 Amid Extreme Market Fear
points: Bitcoin dropped below $60,000 for the first time since June, hitting as low as $58,784 — a 5.9% decline in 24 hours and down from $75,000 over the past week.
Bitcoin is now within 4% of its cycle low (the lowest price reached in the current market period).

Crypto liquidations (forced closing of leveraged trading positions when collateral falls below required levels) surged past $1.5 billion in 24 hours, with 92% being long positions (bets that prices would rise).
The Crypto Fear and Greed Index (a 0-100 scale measuring market sentiment) fell to 9, its lowest reading since February, signaling 'extreme fear.'
Bitcoin formed a 'death cross,' where its 50-day moving average crossed below its 200-day average — a bearish technical signal historically linked to extended downtrends.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs (funds tracking Bitcoin's price for traditional brokerage accounts) saw $582.2 million in outflows Thursday, the largest in three weeks, bringing November's total outflows to $3.5 billion.
This price action contrasts with continued institutional demand: a net $4.11 billion was invested into spot Bitcoin funds during Q3 (third quarter).

unique_angles.point: Market prediction markets now show 74% odds Bitcoin stays below $57,500 by November 30 (up from 26% on Tuesday) and 44% odds it falls to $55,000.
Traders are watching the December 4 jobs report and December 9 Fed meeting, where a 0.25% rate hike is considered nearly certain, adding pressure to risk assets like crypto.

items.title: Wrapped Monero Token Collapses After Hack
points: A wrapped Monero token (a derivative version of the privacy-focused cryptocurrency Monero) lost 99% of its value after a $13 million hack.
Attackers exploited a web hosting vulnerability to drain the deployer's wallet and dump tokens on the market.

items.title: MoonPay Seeks National Trust Bank Charter
points: MoonPay, a major crypto payments firm, applied for a national trust bank charter to expand custody services (secure holding of digital assets) and stablecoin operations.
This follows other crypto companies pursuing federal banking status amid growing political scrutiny.
